parameters.content:
## Publish new Shopify products to Pinterest

> Uses the **PinBridge** community node (`n8n-nodes-pinbridge`), which is verified by n8n and installs on n8n Cloud as well as self-hosted n8n.

### Who's it for
Shopify store owners, and the agencies running their social channels, who want every new product on Pinterest without adding another manual step to launch day.

### How it works
Two Shopify triggers listen for products being created and updated. A product is pinned the first time it is **active, published to your Online Store and has a photo**. Drafts never link to a page that does not exist yet, and a product whose photo is added after it was created still gets its pin.

The pin copy comes from the product's own title, description and price. The workflow downloads the product photo, uploads it to PinBridge as an asset, then publishes the pin by asset ID. Pinterest never has to fetch your CDN at publish time, so a slow, expiring or bot-blocked image URL cannot silently kill the post hours later.

Each pin carries an idempotency key made from the product and board IDs, so a product becomes one pin on that board even when Shopify sends the same event twice. The workflow also remembers which products it has pinned, so later edits skip the download and upload.

Optional: a signed PinBridge webhook sends you a Telegram message when each pin goes live, with its Pinterest link, or when Pinterest refuses one (step 4).

PinBridge handles the Pinterest side end to end - account connection, token refresh, the publish queue, retries and status - so there is no Pinterest API code in this workflow at all.

### How to set up
1. Install the PinBridge community node: Settings -> Community nodes -> search `n8n-nodes-pinbridge`. It is verified by n8n, so it installs on Cloud as well as self-hosted.
2. Connect Shopify with OAuth2: in the Shopify Dev Dashboard, create an app with the `read_products` scope and add the OAuth redirect URL shown in n8n's Shopify OAuth2 credential dialog. Then add that credential to both triggers, and your PinBridge API credential to the PinBridge nodes.
3. Open **Configure your Pinterest settings** and fill in your PinBridge account ID, board ID, store URL and currency.
4. Activate the workflow.
5. Optional: set up the confirmation in step 4.

### How to test
Open **Shopify product created**, click **Listen for test event**, then create an active product with a photo in Shopify. You can also pin a sample product on that trigger and click **Execute workflow**. Either way a real pin is published to your board.

### Requirements
- n8n Cloud or self-hosted n8n
- A PinBridge account with a connected Pinterest profile
- A Shopify store
- Optional: a [Telegram bot](https://telegram.me/BotFather) for the confirmation messages

### How to customize
Rewrite the description lines in **Build the pin title and description** to match your brand voice. To spread launches out instead of posting immediately, change **Publish the pin to Pinterest** to the Schedule resource and set a Run At time.

Shopify sends a product update for every product edit, so expect one short execution per edit. Products that are not ready, or already pinned, stop at **Skip products that aren't ready**.

### 1. Configure

The only node you have to edit: your PinBridge account ID and board ID (PinBridge dashboard, under Accounts and Boards), your store's public URL, and its currency code. Clear the currency to leave prices out of pins.

If a value is still a placeholder, the next node stops the run and says which one.

### 2. Check the product and build the copy

Only products that are active, published to the Online Store and have a photo get through. Drafts, hidden products and products already pinned are dropped; open the filter's output to see the reason for each one.

Pin copy uses the product's own title, description and lowest price, and the alt text of its Shopify photo. No hashtags: Pinterest ranks pins on plain keywords.

### 3. Upload, publish, remember

The photo is uploaded to PinBridge and the pin is published by **asset ID**, not by URL, so an expiring or protected image URL cannot fail the post later.

The idempotency key is the product ID plus the board ID, so replays and duplicate Shopify events still produce one pin. The last node remembers the product so later edits skip the upload.

### 4. Optional: get told when the pin is live

PinBridge calls **PinBridge says a pin is live** when a pin publishes or fails. The signature is checked, other events are dropped, and only pins this workflow created get a message: a Telegram message with the live Pinterest link, or with the reason Pinterest refused the pin. Pins you moved to a schedule are matched too.

To turn it on: activate the workflow, copy the Production URL from the webhook node, pick a signing secret of 16+ characters, and put it and your Telegram chat ID in **Configure the confirmation step**. Then enable **Register the webhook with PinBridge (run once)**, fill in the same URL and secret, run it once, and disable it again. Swap the Telegram node for Slack or Gmail if you prefer.

The signature is recomputed from the parsed body, which matches PinBridge byte for byte while its payloads hold only text fields.
